- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) or neutral, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 1-2 days); cap forecast at +3–4% above recent peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to counteract.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates in high-sentiment periods; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment > 0.33 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) and price is volatile, model tends to lag; add 0.3–0.7% to forecast to catch momentum.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes; if sentiment jumps > 0.50, only adjust forecast if confirmed by 2+ consecutive days.
